vignette: Dipstick shows 3+ blood; microscopy shows no red blood cells; the patient is a marathon runner with muscle pain.
explanation: The dipstick blood pad reacts to heme (RBCs, free hemoglobin AND myoglobin). Positive blood with no RBCs on microscopy in a patient with muscle injury indicates myoglobinuria.

rationales.A: Glomerulonephritis shows dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts on microscopy.
rationales.B: Correct: heme-positive, RBC-negative = hemoglobin/myoglobin; context favors myoglobin.
rationales.C: Menstrual contamination would show actual RBCs.
rationales.D: UTI typically shows LE/nitrite positive and WBCs/bacteria.

misconception: The dipstick cannot distinguish RBCs from hemoglobin or myoglobin — microscopy closes the gap.
